text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Jordanian press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- American brute aggression against Iraq. Jordanian cabinet warns of the consequences of an escalation and rejects any attempt to harm Iraqi sovereignty and the unity of its people and territory.
- Planning Minister Rima Khalaf discusses $100 million loan to Jordan with World Bank and International Monetary Fund.
- Decree to establish royal committee to set up Balqa University in Salt.
- Jordan stock market unworried by U.S. raids on Iraq, prices reach 1996 high.
- Turkish Deputy Prime Minister delays Jordan visit because of events in Iraq.

- Jordan expresses worry over U.S. attacks on Iraq. Crown Prince Hassan says he hopes Iraqi people will emerge from their suffering soon. Prime Minister Abdul Karim al-Kabariti meets Iraqi ambassador and Russian regional envoy.
- Front-page news analysis says Tuesday's U.S. attack may be the "start of the division of Iraq and of civil war".
- Prime Minister Kabariti voices Jordan's rejection of external interfernce in Iraqi affairs.
- Jordanian oposition condemns American "aggression"; most Arab countries condemn U.S. action and urge respect for Iraq's sovereignty.
